name: Carmi
overview: Carmi is a male figure from the tribe of Reuben, identified specifically as a son of Reuben. He appears in the biblical genealogy listing the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational family group that entered Egypt during the patriarchal era. The descendants of Carmi, known as the Carmites, are also noted in the Book of Numbers, linking him to the tribal heritage of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Carmi is a proper name meaning possibly 'fruitful vine' or 'vineyard owner,' reflecting imagery of growth and provision. This meaning, while not explicitly given by God, may suggest a connection to fertility or abundance within the tribal context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Carmi as a son of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. Beyond this direct filial relationship, no further family connections are detailed in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Carmi holds significance primarily as a member of the tribe of Reuben and as one of the sons of Israel who relocated to Egypt, an event that set the stage for the later development of the Israelite nation. His mention alongside the Carmites in Numbers indicates the continuation of his lineage and its role within the tribal organization of Israel. Thus, Carmi contributes to the genealogical and tribal identity foundational to Israel's history.
